title: ADAPT (Adaptive Digital Approaches to Well-Being Promotion Trial): A three-armed randomized controlled trial evaluating the efficacy of two personalized, transdiagnostic mental health products
summary:
Background
Many people experience stress, pressure, or personal difficulties in daily life – even without having a diagnosed mental health condition. Until now, there have been very few digital tools available for these individuals whose effectiveness has been scientifically proven. The ADAPT study examines two new online programs (HelloBetter MindFIT and Ello) designed to help people better cope with everyday stress and improve their personal well-being.

Research Question
The study investigates whether participants in the intervention groups are able to reduce their perceived stress to a significantly greater extent than participants in the control group.

Methodology
Adults aged 18 and older with good German language skills and access to a smartphone are eligible to participate. Participants are randomly assigned to one of three groups: Group 1 uses HelloBetter MindFIT, Group 2 uses Ello, and Group 3 continues their everyday life as usual without using either program. Three online questionnaires are completed: at the start of the study, after 6 weeks, and after 3 months. The study takes place entirely online and does not require any in-person attendance.
conditions: General perceived stress, Mental well-being, Everyday psychological burden

interventions.name:
HelloBetter MindFIT, an online programme for stress management and psychological well-being support.
It is recommended to complete approximately one exercise per day or one module per week. Access to the intervention is granted for 90 days.

Ello, a digital, AI-based application to support users with current challenges and promote mental well-being.
Ello offers unlimited chat and voice-based conversations, with approximately 3 interactions per week recommended. Access to the intervention is granted for 90 days.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Sufficient German language skills (min. C1 level)
Access to a smartphone (min. Android 13 or iOS 18)
Sufficient computer and internet skills
Internet access
Exclusion criteria:
Substantial suicide risk (BDI-II Item 9 > 1)
